title: Readers’ Rides: Adam Sklar’s Tandem is Built From a PBJ Frame
content:
For this week’s Readers’ Rides, we have a special feature from San Francisco-based Sklar Bikes. In recent years, Adam has transitioned from building custom, one-of-one bespoke bicycles for clients to having his designs made in Taiwan, but that doesn’t mean he won’t break out his kit to make random bicycles from time to time in his shop. Let’s check out the latest skunkworks product to roll out of the Farm: a Sklar Tandem…

I built a tandem! Pro tip: if you are looking for a tandem, Craigslist is full of folks looking to get rid of them. So many cool handmade ones from renowned builders for insanely cheap. But unfortunately, I am very vain and had to have one with my name on it, so this project began. Megan and I went on a big group campout earlier this summer, and there were a few tandems there; we had fun cruising them around and thought, sure, why not.

The thing about all these cool old tandems, is a lot of them with wider tires are 90’s and early 2000’s mountain bike geo. Very aggressive and twitchy, and we really just wanted something to cruise through Golden Gate Park and take camping occasionally, so of course the PBJ platform seemed like the move.

Funny enough, this is only my second tandem frame. The last one I built was about a decade ago, and I thought it turned out so nice that I have been thinking about it ever since. That bike was for my old boss Jeff. He so kindly nudged me out of my engineering job and into doing bikes full time, and I ordered a super cool tandem for him and his wife immediately after. Still grateful to him for giving me the encouragement to go full time all those years ago!

Anyhow, this tandem started out with a Medium PBJ frame in the rear. Building a rear end is the hardest part of a bike, and I have enough projects going on, so I chopped off the front end and added my own boom tube and front two triangles. With the PBJ being so popular these days, sometimes I forget that I really became known for my curvy tube bikes. It was fun to pull out the tubing roller and try to make some nice curves on this frame. I think they turned out pretty well!

I also made the Titanium seatpost/stoker stem combo. For the last tandem, I had made an adjustable stem, but I figured we didn’t really need to adjust the stem position that much, and this solution required less machining and welding, so I went with it, and I think it turned out pretty cool!

We are running a SRAM S200 drivetrain with the drive-side timing chain. I didn’t want to deal with finding tandem cranks, so I just spaced out and added another chainring on a spider on the stoker cranks, and it works great. The timing chain is tensioned with a Oner components EBB (PF30). We got some blingy brakes and a stem from Paul Components and are running 29 x 2.6″ Mezcal tires.

Is there a production tandem on the way? The answer is almost definitely no. Just thinking about how to make all the size combos work makes my head spin. Never say never, though…

Some folks have made comments in passing about how it must be much easier to “not be building the bikes anymore,”  a topic we could get deep into because I still do make every single bike in my opinion – but the truth is, running a bike company is way, way more work than being a framebuilder. That said, it feels nice to get back in the shop and weld things, fit things up. Remind myself of what it means to really put a frame together. It is an essential part of my design process and a lot of the special sauce here at Sklar Bikes.

Thanks for looking!
Adam

Build Spec:

  • Frame/Fork: Sklar PBJ Tandem, custom
  • Drive Train: SRAM S200
  • Rims: Stans Flow
  • Hubs: No-name star ratchet
  • Tires: Vittoria Mezcal 29×2.6
  • Handlebars: Sklar PBJ Bar
  • Headset: White Industries spacers, Sklar
  • Crankset: SRAM S200
  • Cassette: SRAM XG-1275 GX Eagle, 10-52t, 12-speed
  • Rear Derailleur: SRAM S200
  • Brakes: Paul Klamper
  • Brake Levers: PAUL Canti Levers
  • Shifter: SRAM
  • Saddles: Brooks Cambium
  • Seatpost: Sklar Titanium one piece Seatpost/stem situation
  • Seatpost: ?? Alloy
  • Stem: PAUL Boxcar
  • Pedals: RaceFace Chester
